events.title: Crafternoon for Adults, Tweens and Teens

cases.refreshed: Come unwind and learn something new at our monthly crafternoon! No experience is necessary. Supplies will be provided, and you're welcome to bring any of your own. In fact some of these crafts may benefit from your personal stash! The activities will be suitable for ages 10 and up. We will have project samples each day to help you visualize the end result. Programs will be on the fourth Sunday of the month. • October – Cardboard Nicho. Recommended items to bring: small images of a cherished item, symbol, memory, or a loved one you miss. • November – Embossing Aluminum Food Charms. Recommended items to bring: colorful Sharpies. • December – Felt and Beaded Patches. Recommended items to bring: old jewelry you don't mind disassembling, beads, colorful thread, loose buttons, scraps of fabric and lace. ¡Ven a relajarte y a aprender algo nuevo en nuestra tarde mensual de artesanías! No se necesita experiencia. Se proporcionarán los materiales, pero puedes traer los que quieras. De hecho, ¡algunas de estas artesanías pueden beneficiarse de tus propios materiales! Las actividades serán aptas para mayores de 10 años. Cada día tendremos ejemplos de proyectos para ayudarte a visualizar el resultado final. • Agosto – Paisaje de playa en collage • Septiembre – Pintura de hongos • Octubre – Nicho de cartón. Materiales recomendados para traer: imágenes pequeñas de un objeto preciado, un símbolo, un recuerdo o un ser querido al que extrañas. • Noviembre – Dijes de aluminio con relieve. Artículos recomendados para traer: marcadores Sharpie de colores, piensa en cuál es tu comida reconfortante. • Diciembre – Parches de fieltro y cuentas. Artículos recomendados para traer: joyas viejas que no te importe desarmar, cuentas, hilo de colores, botones sueltos, retazos de tela y encaje.

events.title: Career Communication Series: Projecting Success through your Nonverbal Communication

cases.refreshed: Our nonverbal communication plays a critical role in our workplace and personal interactions. However, we rarely pause and reflect on how we are presenting ourselves through our tone and body language. This workshop will help you manage your nonverbal communication to have more successful interactions in the workplace and in your personal life. This program is immediately proceeded by: Putting your best face forward: Managing interview questions through the STAR method. In partnership with the SJSU Department of Communication Studies. Free. No registration required. Parking validation for the garage at 88 S. 4th Street will be provided at the program. E-newsletter Signup: Get the inside scoop on business and career resources at SJPL. Sign up today for our monthly e-newsletter, highlighting the latest programs, e-resources and services available at the San José Public Library. #sjplworkscareer

cases.refreshed: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm

cases.refreshed: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes
